body:
## Summary

The MCP `insert` tool needs the full text of every document in `src`. `uri` is only a name: ascot does not read the file. The `insert` description says to "insert every related file, not just the one you're editing", because cross-file references are resolved only against the workspace. So, for cross-file checks, an agent has to read every routine and class in the project and paste them into tool arguments. The CLI (`analyze-workspace`) and the LSP already read the workspace from disk.

`tools/list` is also large: about 28 kB of JSON. Of that, 15.4 kB is the `Style` definition inlined into `create_workspace`, with one property per command and function keyword (195 in all).

## Repro

Any `.mac` file, here `src/DEMO.mac`:

```
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ;
 G NOPE
```

Start `ascot mcp` from the folder that holds `src/`, then call:

```
tools/list
create_workspace {"workspace":"demo"}
insert {"workspace":"demo","files":[{"uri":"src/DEMO.mac"}]}
insert {"workspace":"demo","files":[{"uri":"src/DEMO.mac","src":""}]}
check  {"workspace":"demo","uris":["src/DEMO.mac"]}
```

## Actual (v0.4.3)

```
tools/list          -> 28,253 bytes. create_workspace input schema 17,120, of which $defs.Style 15,434.
                       All input schemas 21,085; output schemas 3,974; descriptions 2,518.
insert without src  -> "failed to deserialize parameters: missing field `src`" (isError: true)
insert with src ""  -> {"affected":["src/DEMO.mac"]}
check               -> A1727 "Syntax error ...
title: MCP: let a workspace load its documents from disk, and shrink the tools/list schema

## Summary

`analyze` and `analyze-workspace` print text only. One diagnostic can span many lines: related information and the token list of a syntax error. On a terminal the `error:`/`warning:` prefix is replaced by a color, so the layout also depends on whether stdout is a TTY. Scripts and CI have to parse that text.

## Repro

`src/DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; sample legacy routine
 Q
SHOW(V) ; print a value
 W V,!
 Q
RUN ; caller passes by reference to a normal parameter
 S X=1
 D SHOW(.X)
 Q
```

`src/DEMOB.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMOB
DEMOB ; sample routine with an unbalanced parenthesis
 K ^TMP(1
 Q
```

```sh
ascot analyze --format json src      # also tried --json, --output-format sarif, --message-format json
ascot analyze src > stdout.txt 2> stderr.txt
```

## Actual (v0.4.3 output; v0.2.0 prints the same)

```text
$ ascot analyze --format json src
error: unexpected argument '--format' found
exit=2
$ ascot analyze src > stdout.txt 2> stderr.txt
exit=1
--- stdout:
warning: src/DEMO.mac:9:9-11 - The parameter 'V' is declared as a normal parameter but got a by-ref argument [A5579]
- src/DEMO.mac:4:6-7: Parameter declared here — add `&` (routine label) or `ByRef` (method) to declare it by-ref.
warning: src/DEMOB.mac:4:2-3 - Syntax error, looking for:
parse error at byte 32, expected:
	- "#"
	- "'"
	- ")"
	- ","
	- "?"
	- "\n"
	- Char of not line breaking whitespace
	- LineComment
	- Operator
	- RangeComment
 [A1727]
--- stderr:
2 diagnostic(s)
title: Machine-readable output for `ascot analyze` (JSON, and SARIF for code scanning)

body:
## Summary

There is no way to turn a diagnostic code off, or to report only some codes. `analyze`, `analyze-workspace` and `lsp` take only `--iris`, `--iris-namespace` and `--style`, and the MCP `create_workspace` call takes only `iris`, `iris_namespace` and `style`. There is no config file and no suppression comment.

The `ascot-lsp` Claude Code plugin starts `ascot lsp` with no arguments (`"args": ["lsp"]`), so even those three options cannot reach it.

Diagnostic codes were added (#62, #69, #67) so that clients can filter by kind. Here the clients are the ascot CLI and the bundled plugin, and neither can filter.

## Repro

`src/DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; sample legacy routine
 Q
SHOW(V) ; print a value
 W V,!
 Q
RUN ; caller passes by reference to a normal parameter (legal, and common in old code)
 S X=1
 D SHOW(.X)
 Q
```

```sh
ascot analyze src
ascot analyze --ignore A5579 src     # also tried --disable, --select, --allow
echo '{"ignore":["A5579"]}' > style.json && ascot analyze --style style.json src
```

A trailing comment such as `; ascot-ignore A5579` on line 9 changes nothing.

## Actual (v0.4.3 output; v0.2.0 prints the same)

```text
$ ascot analyze src
warning: src/DEMO.mac:9:9-11 - The parameter 'V' is declared as a normal parameter but got a by-ref argument [A5579]
- src/DEMO.mac:4:6-7: Parameter declared here — add `&` (routine label) or `ByRef` (method) to declare it by-ref.
1 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
exit=1
$ ascot analyze --igno
title: Select or suppress diagnostic codes, in the CLI, the LSP and the ascot-lsp plugin

body:
## Summary

ascot accepts `$ZU(...)` and `$ZUTIL(...)` calls without any diagnostic. Many of these calls have documented replacements, for example `$ZU(5)` is `$NAMESPACE` and `$ZU(68,40,n)` is `$SYSTEM.Process.SetZEOF(n)`. ascot does report an unknown function such as `$ZFOO`, so the gap is only for `$ZUTIL`.

## Repro

`DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; superseded $ZUTIL calls
 quit
NS() ; current namespace
 quit $ZU(5)
NS2() ; the same, long form
 quit $ZUTIL(5)
ZEOF() ; process end-of-file handling
 new old
 set old=$ZU(68,40,1)
 quit old
BAD() ; an unknown function, for contrast
 quit $ZFOO(1)
```

```sh
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
```

No IRIS connection is needed.

## Actual (v0.4.3)

```
error: DEMO.mac:13:7-15 - $ZFOO is not a recognized function; did you mean: ZF, F, ZBOOLEAN, ZCOS, ZCOT? [A3850]
1 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
```

Lines 5, 7 and 10 get nothing. If you remove the `$ZFOO` line, the file reports `0 diagnostic(s)` and exits 0. v0.2.0 gives the same output. A class method that returns `$ZUTIL(5)` also gets nothing.

## Expected

A warning or hint on each `$ZU`/`$ZUTIL` call that has a documented replacement, with the replacement in the message, for example:

- `$ZU(5)`: use `$NAMESPACE`
- `$ZU(68,40,n)`: use `$SYSTEM.Process.SetZEOF(n)`

The mapping could follow the published `$ZUTIL` replacement list. The InterSystems Language Server uses that list for its diagnostic ("`$ZUTIL` functions that are deprecated or have been superseded", intersys
title: No diagnostic for superseded $ZUTIL calls such as $ZU(5) and $ZU(68,40,n)

## Summary

With no IRIS connection, ascot reports every call to a routine that is not in the workspace with the A3303 warning. That includes system routines such as `%ETN`, which every namespace has. A `%` class in the same situation is trusted, or gets a hint.

The README ("Connecting to IRIS") says: "Without a connection, such a class or routine is left unconfirmed (a hint, not an error)". For routines this is not what happens: the diagnostic is a warning, and `ascot analyze` exits non-zero on a warning.

## Repro

`DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; sample routine
 Q
TRAP ; error trap
 D ^%ETN
 D LOG^%ETN
 Q
VER() ; a system class, for comparison
 Q ##class(%SYSTEM.Version).GetVersion()
MISS ; a routine that does not exist, for comparison
 D ^NOSUCH
 Q
```

```sh
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
```

No `--iris`. macOS, release binary `ascot-cli-universal-apple-darwin`.

## Actual

```
warning: DEMO.mac:5:4-9 - Cannot find routine '%ETN' in this workspace, with no IRIS connection to check it against [A3303]
warning: DEMO.mac:6:4-12 - Cannot find routine '%ETN' in this workspace, with no IRIS connection to check it against [A3303]
warning: DEMO.mac:11:4-11 - Cannot find routine 'NOSUCH' in this workspace, with no IRIS connection to check it against [A3303]
3 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
```

Exit code 1. The system class call gets no diagnostic. The system routine gets the same warning as the missing one, once per call.

v0.2.0 reported the same calls as errors ("Rout
title: Without an IRIS connection, a call to a system routine such as `^%ETN` is a warning; the README says hint
Status macros ($$$OK, $$$ISERR, ...) in a class are reported undefined (A2797, error) when run without --iris

body:
## Summary

A label or method can take an array by reference and start with `KILL x` to clear it before filling it. ascot then reports A5718 "Variable 'x' is assigned but never read" at the parameter declaration. The caller reads the result, so nothing goes unread. A routine label has no `Output` keyword, so no declaration avoids the warning.

## Repro

`src/DEMOOUT.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMOOUT
FILL(&x) public {
    kill x
    set x("a") = 1
    quit
}
FILLNOKILL(&x) public {
    set x("a") = 1
    quit
}
USE() public {
    do FILL(.r), FILLNOKILL(.s)
    write r("a"), s("a"),!
    quit
}
```

`src/Demo.Out.cls`:

```objectscript
Class Demo.Out [ Abstract ]
{

ClassMethod FillByRef(ByRef x As %String)
{
    kill x
    set x("a") = 1
}

ClassMethod FillOutput(Output x As %String)
{
    kill x
    set x("a") = 1
}

}
```

Command:

```
ascot analyze src/
```

## Actual (v0.4.3)

```
warning: src/DEMOOUT.mac:2:7-8 - Variable 'x' is assigned but never read [A5718]
warning: src/Demo.Out.cls:4:23-41 - Variable 'x' is assigned but never read [A5718]
2 diagnostic(s) across 2 file(s)
```

v0.2.0 gives the same output. Only the `KILL` triggers it. `FILLNOKILL` and `FillOutput` are not reported, and neither is a by-ref parameter overwritten with `set x = 5`.

## Expected

No A5718 for a by-reference parameter, because its value goes back to the caller. In a routine label there is nothing to report. In a method, a hint that `Output` fits better than `ByRef` would be accurate. "
title: A5718 "assigned but never read" on a by-reference parameter that is killed before it is filled

body:
## Summary

Passing a variable by reference (`.x`) to a label or method whose formal parameter has no `&` or `ByRef` is legal. The callee gets the variable by reference and its changes reach the caller. ascot reports A5579 as a warning at every such call, and the related note says to add `&` or `ByRef` "to declare it by-ref".

The documentation describes both markers as having no effect:

- RCOS, Symbols Used in ObjectScript, `&`: "In a formal parameter list, an optional, non-functional variable name prefix that marks a parameter as one that should be passed by reference."
- GOBJ 7.5, Indicating How Arguments Are to Be Passed: "The ByRef and Output keywords provide information for the benefit of anyone using the InterSystems Class Reference. They do not affect the behavior of the code."

The comment above the check in `src/check/mod.rs` says the same: "the caller's `.` alone decides by-reference; `ByRef`/`Output` document intent".

Older routines rarely use `&`, so a helper that takes a counter or seed by reference gives one warning per call site.

## Repro

`DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; by-reference argument passed to a plain formal parameter
    quit
MAIN() public {
    set seed = 42
    set a = $$NEXT(.seed)
    write a, " ", seed, !
    quit
}
NEXT(seed) public {
    set seed = seed + 1
    quit seed
}
OLD ; older style, no procedure block
    S X=1,Y=$$NXT(.X) W X," ",Y,!
    Q
NXT(N) S N=N+1 Q N
```

```
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
```

## Actual

```
warn
title: A5579 warns on every `.var` argument to a plain formal parameter, which is legal and works

body:
## Summary

In a WRITE command, only plain expression arguments are checked. The expression after `?` (tab), `*` (character code) and `*-` (device control) is skipped. As a result:

- A7155 (left-to-right precedence) is not reported inside `?(...)`.
- An undefined variable or a missing label inside these arguments is not reported.
- A variable read only inside `?(...)` is reported as "assigned but never read" (A5718).

## Repro

`DEMO.mac` (one case per label):

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; WRITE ?expr and *expr arguments, one case per label
    quit
PLAIN(n) public {
    write n - 1 * 12, !
    quit
}
TAB(n) public {
    write ?(n - 1 * 12), "x", !
    quit
}
TABUNDEF() public {
    write ?(undefinedcol), "x", !
    quit
}
TABLABEL() public {
    write ?$$NOSUCH(), "x", !
    quit
}
CHARUNDEF() public {
    write *undefinedchar
    quit
}
OLD(N) W ?(N-1*12),"x",!
    Q
```

```
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
```

## Actual

```
warning: DEMO.mac:5:11-21 - ObjectScript has no operator precedence and evaluates strictly left-to-right; this may not compute what you expect [A7155]
warning: DEMO.mac:8:5-6 - Variable 'n' is assigned but never read [A5718]
warning: DEMO.mac:24:5-6 - Variable 'N' is assigned but never read [A5718]
3 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
```

The same file with `?` and `*` removed (so each expression is a plain WRITE argument) gives A7155 on lines 9 and 24, A7095 on lines 13 and 21, and A6851 on line 17.

`write *-nosuch` and `write /CUP(nosuch, 1)` give no d
title: WRITE `?expr`, `*expr` and `*-expr` arguments are not checked

body:
## Summary

When a `GOTO` or `DO` target has an offset (`LABEL+n`), ascot does not look the label up.

- `G NOPE+3` and `D NOPE+1` are not reported. `G NOPE` is reported (A6851).
- `G LBL+99`, past the end of the routine, is not reported.
- `references` on a label (LSP and MCP) does not list `G LBL+3`, `D LBL+2` or `D LBL+1^DEMO`.
- `definition` at those call sites returns null.

## Repro

`src/DEMO.mac`:

```
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; label+offset demo
 Q
LBL ; four lines
 S X=1
 S X=2
 S X=3
 Q
OK0 ; plain call (control)
 D LBL
 Q
OK1 ; valid offset, GOTO
 G LBL+3
OK2 ; valid offset, DO
 D LBL+2
 Q
BAD1 ; no such label, GOTO with offset
 G NOPE+3
BAD2 ; no such label, DO with offset
 D NOPE+1
 Q
BAD3 ; offset past the end of the routine
 G LBL+99
CONTROL ; no such label, no offset (control)
 G NOPE
```

CLI:

```
ascot analyze src/
```

LSP (`ascot lsp`, workspace root `src/`) and MCP (`ascot mcp`, after `create_workspace` and `insert` of the file), positions zero-based:

- `references` at line 3, character 0 (the label `LBL`)
- `definition` at line 12, character 3 (`G LBL+3`) and line 14, character 3 (`D LBL+2`)

Cross-routine, add `src/DEMO2.mac`:

```
ROUTINE DEMO2
DEMO2 ;
 D LBL^DEMO
 D LBL+1^DEMO
 D NOPE+1^DEMO
 D NOPE^DEMO
 Q
```

## Actual (v0.4.3)

v0.2.0 gives the same output for every check below.

CLI on `DEMO.mac`: only the control line is reported.

```
error: src/DEMO.mac:25:2-8 - Cannot find label 'NOPE' in this routine [A6851]
1 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
```
title: Label+offset targets (`GOTO LABEL+n`, `DO LABEL+n`) are not resolved: missing labels pass, and references/definition skip them

body:
## Summary

When a label, procedure or method has two independent defects, only the first is reported. Once a statement produces a diagnostic, the later statements in the same body are not checked. Fix the first, run again, and the second appears. Inside an `if { }` block the stop is limited to that block: statements after the block are still checked.

This also happens when the first diagnostic is only a warning. A7155 (precedence) and A6705 (too few arguments) are warnings, but they still stop the check, so a warning can hide an error such as an undefined variable.

## Repro

`DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
DEMO ; two independent defects in one procedure
    quit
TWO() public {
    set total = $$ADD(1, 2, 3)
    write total, " ", totl, !
    quit
}
WARNFIRST(n) public {
    set x = n - 1 * 12
    write x, totl, !
    quit
}
ONLYUNDEF() public {
    set total = $$ADD(1, 2)
    write total, " ", totl, !
    quit
}
ADD(a, b) public {
    quit a + b
}
```

```
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
```

## Actual

```
error: DEMO.mac:5:29-30 - Too many arguments [A5523]
warning: DEMO.mac:10:13-23 - ObjectScript has no operator precedence and evaluates strictly left-to-right; this may not compute what you expect [A7155]
error: DEMO.mac:16:23-27 - This value is undefined: totl [A7095]
3 diagnostic(s) across 1 file(s)
```

`totl` is undefined on lines 6, 11 and 16, but only line 16 is reported. In `TWO` the A5523 hides it, and in `WARNFIRST` the A7155 warning hides it. With the first de
title: The first diagnostic in a label or method stops the rest of its body from being checked

body:
## Summary

ascot reports the hint A4043 "Type checking not implemented for ..." on a stand-alone `ELSE`,
an argumentless `DO` and a dotted line. After that hint, nothing else in the same label or
procedure is checked. Undefined variables, missing labels and unknown functions after it are not
reported, and neither are `--style` warnings. The next label is checked again.

A stand-alone `ELSE` here is one that does not follow an `IF` on the line before, for example
after a timed `LOCK` or `READ`. Both forms are valid and common in older routines. The same code
written with `if '$test { ... }` is checked.

## Repro

`DEMO.mac`:

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMO
WithElse(count) public {
    lock +^Demo(count):5
    else  quit 0
    set total = cuont + 1
    quit total
}
WithTest(count) public {
    lock +^Demo(count):5
    if '$test { quit 0 }
    set total = cuont + 1
    quit total
}
```

`DEMOL.mac` (labels without procedure blocks):

```objectscript
ROUTINE DEMOL
AFTERELSE ; stand-alone ELSE after a timed LOCK
 L +^Demo(1):5
 E  Q 0
 D MISSING
 Q 1
AFTERDO ; argumentless DO with a dotted block
 D
 . S X=1
 D MISSING
 Q
AFTERIFDO ; the same behind an IF
 I $D(^Demo) D
 . S X=1
 D MISSING
 Q
CONTROL ; neither
 D MISSING
 Q
```

```
ascot analyze DEMO.mac
ascot analyze DEMOL.mac
```

## Actual

v0.4.3 (v0.2.0 prints the same):

```
$ ascot analyze DEMO.mac
hint: DEMO.mac:4:5-17 - Type checking not implemented for 'Stand-alone Else Command' [A4043]
error: DEMO.mac:11:17-22 - This val
title: Checking and --style stop for the rest of a label after a stand-alone ELSE or an argumentless DO (A4043)

body:
### Problem

When a routine isn't in the workspace and IRIS has no `.int` or `.mac` source for it, ascot can't tell whether the routine is missing or exists with only its OBJ, so it reports every such call with the same hedged warning:

```
warning: Demo.cls:7:10-20 - Cannot find routine 'MyLib.Util' in this workspace, and IRIS has no source for it: it is missing, or IRIS has only its OBJ [A3303]
```

A typo in a routine name gets the same warning as a call into a routine IRIS ships compiled only.

### Proposed solutions

IRIS can tell the two apart: `%Library.RoutineMgr_StudioOpenDialog` with the spec `MyLib.Util.mac,MyLib.Util.int,MyLib.Util.obj` lists the routine's OBJ when it exists, and nothing when it doesn't (the InterSystems Language Server's routine completion uses the same query).

Make `get-int-or-mac`'s answer richer than `option<routine-source>`: the source, OBJ only, missing, or couldn't check (e.g. a host with no server). Then:

- Source: check the call against the routine's labels, as now.
- OBJ only: check the call as untyped, with a hint that it can't be checked precisely.
- Missing: an error, as for a class missing on IRIS.
- Couldn't check, or no IRIS connection: the current warning.

Declaration files would record OBJ-only routines too, so `--iris <file>` answers the same way.
title: Tell a missing routine from one IRIS has only as OBJ

    For {
        Set child = ..Children.GetNext(.key)
        Quit:key=""
        Set names = names_child.Name
    }
    Quit names
}

}
```

`Demo/Child.cls`:

```objectscript
Class Demo.Child Extends %Persistent
{

Property Name As %String;

Relationship Owner As Demo.Parent [ Cardinality = one, Inverse = Children ];

}
```

```sh
ascot analyze --iris http://user:pass@localhost:8080/iris --iris-namespace USER Demo
```

### What did you observe?

```
error: Demo/Parent.cls:12:33-37 - Cannot find member 'Name' in %RelationshipObject; did you mean: CLASSNAMEINOID, %New, %NormalizeObject, %OnValidateObject, Normalize, %GetParameter, %GetSerial, %GetSwizzleObject? [A3139]
1 diagnostic(s) across 2 file(s)
```

### What do you expect?

No diagnostic. `..Children.GetNext(.key)` returns a `Demo.Child`, which has `Name`.
title: A relationship's GetNext result is typed as the relationship, so its members are reported missing

### Problem

Diagnostics only carry a message and a severity, so a client can't tell one kind of finding from another: the Problems panel can't filter by kind, and a quick fix has nothing stable to key on.

### Proposed solutions

Add `code` and `code-description` to the WIT `diagnostic` record, and pass them through the LSP as `code` and `codeDescription.href`.

- `code`: a fixed code per `TypeErrorKind` variant, e.g. `A2797`, assigned once and never reused, so renaming a kind or rewording its message doesn't change it.
- `code-description`: that variant's entry on docs.rs for the running version, which needs `TypeErrorKind` to be public.
title: Diagnostics: add a code and a docs link to each diagnostic

body:
### Problem

A diagnostic's `codeDescription` link opens its kind's entry in `TypeErrorKind` on docs.rs, which shows only the kind's code. The message text lives in a separate `Display` match, so documenting a kind means restating its message in a second place, where the two can drift.

### Proposed solutions

Make each variant's doc comment the single source: its first paragraph is the message template, any later paragraphs an optional explanation. `type_error_kinds!` generates `Display` from the template, passing each field by name:

```rust
/// The macro '{name}' is undefined{suggestions}
///
/// Optional: why it matters, an example, how to fix it.
#[code = "A2797"]
UndefinedMacro { name: String, suggestions: Suggestions },
```

A scratch-crate test confirmed `write!(f, $msg, name = name)` works through `macro_rules!`. What it takes:

- Named fields for every variant (about 25 are tuple variants today).
- Small `Display` types for the conditional parts of messages: the "did you mean" list, `InconsistentDeclaration`'s "declared as"/"undeclared", `InvalidSyntax`'s friendly error text, and `UnconfirmedClass`'s two sentences.
- Every field must appear in its template; an unused named argument fails to compile.
- Trimming the leading space a `/// ` line produces.

Codes, variant names, and messages stay unchanged.
title: Generate diagnostic messages from TypeErrorKind's doc comments

body:
### Problem

Diagnostics only carry a message and a severity, so a client can't tell one kind of finding from another. The Problems panel can't filter, for example, style warnings (#55) out from among semantic errors, and a future quick fix has nothing stable to key on. Nothing links a diagnostic to documentation either.

Thanks @isc-uuill for inspiration.

### Proposed solutions

Add optional `code` and `code-description` fields to the WIT `diagnostic` record, and pass them through the LSP as `code` and `codeDescription.href`.

- `code`: the `TypeErrorKind` variant's name in kebab case, e.g. `keyword-style`.
- `code-description`: that variant's rustdoc on docs.rs, so its doc comment is the description. For example, `https://docs.rs/ascot/<version>/ascot/check/enum.TypeErrorKind.html#variant.KeywordStyle`, with `<version>` from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` so the link matches the running build.

The second needs `TypeErrorKind` to be public; it isn't on docs.rs today. A `missing_docs` lint on it would keep every code documented.
title: Diagnostics: add `code` and `codeDescription`

body:
### Problem

Every `--iris` run resolves the system and library classes, include files and routines it meets over a live IRIS connection. A workflow without one, CI for example, can't resolve them at all.

### Proposed solutions

1. A CLI subcommand that writes a namespace's declarations to a file once: for every class, its superclasses, members, signatures and types, as `get_cls` reports them over a live connection; for every `.inc` file and routine, its source, as `get_inc`/`get_int_or_mac` would fetch it. The file is the `iris-connection` interface as data. "Declaration" in the sense other type checkers use it: an implementation-free description of code to check against.

   ```sh
   ascot declare --iris http://user:password@localhost:8080/iris --iris-namespace USER user.d.json
   ```

2. Let `--iris` (on `analyze`, `analyze-workspace`, `lsp`, and the MCP `iris` argument) take the path of such a file instead of a URL, so a run needs no IRIS connection:

   ```sh
   ascot analyze --iris user.d.json <PATH>...
   ```
title: Declaration files: write a namespace to a file once, so `--iris` needs no REST traffic
